summary: Halyard mutual NDA with Pravah Infotech carrying counterparty edits that strip advisers, auditors, insurers and Group from permitted recipients, add a logo-use right, add an uncapped indemnity, and a residuals request, plus a request to shorten survival.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party undertakes to the Disclosing Party that it shall:
findings.why: Obligations bind the Receiving Party and Disclosing Party is defined so either Party can be either.

findings.quote: which is either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of its disclosure
findings.why: Definition covers information disclosed for the Purpose, marked or reasonably confidential, and includes derived notes and analyses.

findings.quote: specifically the evaluation of a potential software integration and offshore development partnership
findings.why: The inserted wording limits the Purpose to a named evaluation project and clause 2.1.2 restricts use solely to the Purpose.
findings.fallback_cited: Purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.

findings.quote: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.why: All four carve-outs are present, unnarrowed, with a written records or reasonable evidence standard.

findings.quote: [[DEL: , professional advisers, auditors and insurers]]
findings.why: Deleting professional advisers, auditors and insurers from Representatives means no disclosure to them is permitted.
findings.draft_redline: Representatives means, in relation to a Party, the employees, officers, directors, professional advisers, auditors and insurers of that Party and of any member of its Group.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We need to be able to share information with our professional advisers, auditors and insurers on a need-to-know basis, so we have reinstated them. The same permission applies equally to you.

findings.quote: [[DEL:  and of any member of its Group]]
findings.why: Group members are removed from Representatives and from clause 4.1, with no consent mechanism for Group disclosure.
findings.draft_redline: Reinstate 'and members of its Group' in clauses 1.1.7, 4.1, 4.1.1, 4.1.2, 4.1.3 and 6.1.2, so disclosure to Group members is permitted on a need-to-know basis.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Group members are covered on a need-to-know basis, with the Receiving Party liable for them, so we have reinstated this wording. This applies equally to your affiliates.

findings.quote: 5.2 Before making any disclosure pursuant to Clause 5.1, the Receiving Party shall, to the extent that it is legally permitted to do so:
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice and cooperation apply only where legally permitted, and resisting disclosure is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within [[DEL: ten]][[INS: fifteen (15)]] Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: Fifteen Business Days is a period of 5 Business Days or more; officer confirmation and backup/legal retention exceptions in 6.1.3 and 6.2 remain.
findings.fallback_cited: Any period of 5 Business Days or more.

findings.quote: No right or licence, express or implied, is granted to the Receiving Party or any of its Representatives in respect of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information
findings.why: All Confidential Information and IP stays with the Disclosing Party and no licence beyond use for the Purpose is granted.

findings.quote: we normally include a standard residuals clause confirming that our personnel are free to use general skills, know-how and experience retained in their unaided memories
findings.why: The counterparty asks for a residuals right to use information retained in unaided memory, which the playbook does not permit in any form.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Thank you for raising this. We are unable to include a residuals clause, as our standard position is that Confidential Information may be used solely for the Purpose. We hope you understand.

findings.quote: Neither Party makes any representation or gives any warranty, express or implied, as to the accuracy, completeness, adequacy or fitness for a particular purpose of any Confidential Information
findings.why: Information is 'as is', no warranty, no reliance liability except fraud, and no obligation to proceed.

findings.quote: provided, however, that Counterparty shall have the right to include Halyard's name and corporate logo in its standard customer and partner lists, pitch decks, and marketing materials
findings.why: The insertion lets the Counterparty use Halyard's name and logo publicly without consent, one-sidedly.
findings.draft_redline: Delete the proviso beginning '; provided, however, that Counterparty shall have the right to include Halyard's name and corporate logo...' so that clause 8.1 ends after 'in accordance with Clause 5'.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are not able to agree to use of our name or logo in customer lists or marketing materials at the NDA stage. We are happy to revisit this in any future commercial agreement.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: Personal data is limited to business contact details and any other sharing requires a separate DPA first.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Term is 2 years with 30 days' notice, survival is 3 years, and Trade Secrets are protected while they remain Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: we request that the post-termination survival period be reduced to two (2) years from the date of expiry or termination
findings.why: A 2-year survival period is within the acceptable 2 to 5 year range, and Trade Secret protection is retained in clause 10.3.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief for any threatened or actual breach of this Agreement by the other Party
findings.why: Mutual right to seek injunctive and equitable relief, with remedies cumulative in 11.2.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Disclosing Party from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, costs and expenses
findings.why: The inserted wording adds an uncapped indemnity for any breach, and the playbook allows no indemnity of any kind.
findings.draft_redline: Delete the inserted sentence beginning 'In addition, the Receiving Party shall indemnify...' so clause 11.2 reads: 'The rights and remedies provided under this Agreement are cumulative and do not exclude any rights or remedies provided by law.'
findings.note_to_counterparty: We do not include indemnities in our NDA, as liability for breach is left to general law, so we have removed this sentence.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer, mortgage, charge, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner with any or all of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party.
findings.why: No assignment without prior written consent, applying to both Parties.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: English law and exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales are unchanged.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure of any software, prototypes or other tangible objects
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes remains prohibited.
